title: Professional Error Handling
outcome: Create a stable application error model that separates expected domain/transport failures from unexpected faults and keeps diagnostics observable.
artifact: Error taxonomy + NestJS mapping layer/filters + structured error response with request IDs.
labSteps: Inventory current TaskFlow failures and group them into validation, auth, forbidden, missing, conflict, infrastructure, and unexpected categories.
Create explicit application errors for expected business outcomes rather than throwing arbitrary strings.
Map errors to one stable HTTP envelope at a central boundary.
Add request/correlation IDs to responses and logs.
Trigger each error class intentionally and verify both client-safe response and server diagnostic context.
Prove an unexpected exception returns a generic 500 while the real stack/context remains in logs.
failureModes: Using one generic 400 for semantically different failures
mastery: Can distinguish expected vs unexpected errors
Can trace a request by ID
Can design frontend recovery from stable error codes
principles: Map known failures to stable HTTP error responses instead of leaking raw exceptions.
Keep unexpected errors observable to operators while returning safe messages to clients.
Use consistent error shapes so frontend code does not branch on dozens of unrelated formats.
Preserve enough context in logs to diagnose an error without sending secrets to the browser.
